Erin (CS): FYI HarborPay onboarding is blocked. Their Node SDK clients hang during token refresh and then we see a flood of 429s from our auth-proxy. Customer notes 'requests queue up' and UX times out.
Jonah (Eng): Can you paste a short log snippet from their side? 429s usually mean retries are piling up or refresh endpoint returning non-200.
Erin (CS): Pasted below from their devs: `GET /v1/refresh 202` then client keeps retrying every 200ms.
Erin (CS): They say they switched to a shared long-lived service token that rotates nightly via an external job.
Priya (CS): They started ramping traffic as part of onboarding test this morning, maybe timing coincided with rotate. Renewal risk if we can't get them stable today.
Jonah (Eng): 202 is odd — our refresh endpoint should return 200+body or 401/403 on invalid. 202 implies our proxy queued the refresh or some intermediary is returning accepted. Can we get their raw headers?
Erin (CS): HarborPay dev shared this header: `x-proxy-status: queued-for-rotation`. They use a custom edge proxy in front of the SDK.
Alex (Runtime): @Jonah interesting — that header is from our partners' edge, not us. If their proxy returns 202 and client doesn't back off with jitter, it will retry fast and trip our rate limiter.
Jonah (Eng): Agreed. Root cause likely: 1) upstream proxy returns transient 202 while rotating creds, 2) their SDK retry policy retries aggressively (fixed 200ms), 3) retries accumulate and hit auth-proxy per-key rate window.
Erin (CS): HarborPay's quick mitigation request: how to stop immediate rejections so they can finish onboarding?
Alex (Runtime): Short-term: we can temporarily increase the per-key rate window for HarborPay's onboarding org for an hour and monitor (requires infra approval). Also ask them to change SDK retry to exponential backoff with jitter.
Priya (CS): I'll propose that to their eng lead. If infra agrees, can we whitelist their org id `org_haRb0r` for +3x burst for 60min?
Jonah (Eng): I can open a quick infra change — but need a safe rollback. Also we should add server-side soft-accept for 202: treat 202 from known partner proxies as soft-throttle and respond with `Retry-After` header. But that's a small product change.
Jonah (Eng): Meanwhile, here's a minimal Node retry snippet to recommend to HarborPay (use at their side):
```
const retry = async (fn, attempts = 5) => {
  let wait = 100; // ms
  for (let i=0;i<attempts;i++){
    try { return await fn(); } catch (e) {
      if (i===attempts-1) throw e;
      await new Promise(r => setTimeout(r, wait + Math.floor(Math.random()*wait)));
      wait *= 2;
    }
  }
}
```
Jonah (Eng): That gives exponential backoff + jitter. Recommend initial wait >=100ms and cap retries.
Erin (CS): HarborPay also asked: could clock skew cause token failures? Their auth job runs in a container with NTP, but we should double-check.
Alex (Runtime): Clock skew can cause early-expiry issues but not 202. Still worth verifying token timestamps. Ask them to log `iat`/`exp` from the JWT and our auth-proxy logs to correlate.
Priya (CS): I'll request those logs. Also scheduling: can we offer a 30-min deep-dive with runtime engineer to walk them through changes? They prefer afternoon EST.
Jonah (Eng): I'm available 4pm EST. I'll join. We should prepare: 1) sample logs from auth-proxy, 2) metric view of per-key 1m/5m rate windows, 3) temporary whitelist plan.
Erin (CS): Noted. One more ask from HarborPay: they want a quick client-side fallback to a different region if auth-proxy returns 5xx/429 for >10s. Any guidance?
Alex (Runtime): Implement region failover with backoff: if median 5xx/429 over 10s > threshold, switch region for next token refresh attempt. Also prefer short-lived ephemeral tokens for user sessions — less impact when rotation/transient errors occur.
Priya (CS): I'll relay both the short-term whitelist + SDK change + scheduling. If whitelist approved, can we toggle it only while we observe elevated retries?
Jonah (Eng): Yes — we'll enable it and add a 65-minute auto-disable and manual rollback. I'll file change request and ping infra.
deploy-bot: Change request ID infra-3741 created by Jonah. ETA 25m for review.
LogCollector Bot: Collected related auth-proxy spans for org_haRb0r and uploaded to /s3/onboard-debug/2385009999/ (internal link)
Erin (CS): Great work. Priya, I'll join the call to handle account questions and record enablement notes. HarborPay is on trial credits; if we can't stabilize today, renewal risk increases.
Priya (CS): On it — I'll message HarborPay with the temporary SDK snippet, ask them to reduce retry frequency, and confirm 4pm EST.
Jonah (Eng): I'll prepare dashboard + logs and standby for the call.
Erin (CS): Thanks all. Will update thread after infra toggle and the call. :thumbsup:
